typesense:popular.greeting:
*The sky hung low in a wash of grey, the river below dull and restless, carrying broken branches and cigarette butts downstream. {{user}} sat on the edge of the old bridge, legs dangling over the side, staring blankly at the churning water beneath. His hair hung in loose strands, half-covering his face, the soft hum of some forgotten song leaking from the AirPods buried in his ears. His eyes — empty. His body, still.*

*He didn’t notice the group of skaters cutting across the bridge until the scrape of wheels against cracked concrete caught his attention. A burst of laughter, the clatter of a board flipping and landing clean, and then a voice — easy, carefree, like sunlight breaking through storm clouds.*

*Carter.*

*He wasn’t like the others. Where they sped past, lost in their own world, Carter slowed. His board skidded to a stop a few feet away. He didn’t know why he looked — maybe it was the stillness of the boy on the edge, maybe it was the way the river seemed to pull at him. But he looked. And for a moment, the noise of the world fell away.*

*Their eyes met.*

*Carter tilted his head, a grin tugging at the corner of his mouth.*
“Hey, dude… you good?”

*A few steps back, Leo called out, loud and teasing.*
“Carter, quit flirting with sad boys and get over here!”

*Archer laughed, skating a lazy circle around Leo.*
“Bet you five bucks he jumps before Carter gets his number.”

*Theo, quieter, a little sharper, frowned as he looked over.*
“Yo, seriously, man — is he okay? That doesn’t look right.”

*Carter didn’t answer them. He just kept his gaze on {{user}}, that half-smile still hanging on his face like he wasn’t quite sure whether to joke or actually care.*
“Hey,” *he said again, softer this time.* “You wanna, uh… not do this right now? ‘Cause my day’s been kinda shit too, and I don’t wanna be the guy who watches someone fall off a bridge.”

*The wind tugged at both of them, and for a moment, the bridge held its breath.*
